4. So far as the ratification of Martial Law Proclamations, Regulations, Orders, acts and actions since 15th August, 1975 is .concerned paragraph (3a) to the Schedule of the Constitution of Bangladesh inserted by the Proclamation Order No. I of 1977 says that all such Proclamations, Regulations, Orders acts and actions shall be deemed to have been validly made. Paragraph 18 the aforesaid 4th Schedule added under Act I of 1979 being the 5th Amendment of the Constitution says that all such Martial Law Proclamations, Regulations, Orders, acts and actions made between 15th August, 1975 and 9th April, 1979, both days inclusive, have been ratified, confirmed and declared to have been validly made, done or taken. What is important to note is the exact specific period ascribed in added paragraph 18 to the 4th Schedule of the Constitution by Act I of 1979. In this connection the relevant dates of the last Proclamation of Martial Law and Act I of 1979 are very much relevant. Last Proclamation of Martial Law for withdrawal of Martial Law was issued on 6th April, 1979 to be effective from 8 P.M. of 6th April, 1979 though published in the Extra Ordinary Gazette of the Government of Bangladesh on 7th April, 1979, whereas Act I of 1979 being the 5th Amendment of the Constitution adding paragraph 18 to the 4th Schedule of the Constitution was finally enacted on 6th April, 1979 on receipt of the assent of the President and was published in the Extraordinary Gazette of the Government of Bangladesh on 6th April, 1979. Thus it would appear that both the last Proclamation of Mart al Law and Act I of 1979 saving the Martial Law were issued on the same day, that is 6th April, 1979. The specific period ascribed in the last Material Law Proclamation for saving all Martial Law Proclamations, Regulations, Orders, acts and actions however extended beyond the period from the date and time of the withdrawal of Martial Law at 8 P.M. of 6th April, 1979 up to 9th April 1979. This only shows that even the last Proclamation of Martial Law wherein Martial Law was finally withdrawn with effect from 8 P.M. on 6th April, 1979 issued on 6th April, 1979 and published in the Extraordinary Gazette on 7th April, was also saved and ratified by the Parliament under Act I of 1979 being the 5th Amendment of the Constitution by way of addition of paragraph 18 to the 4th Schedule of the Constitution.. Taking into consideration the period ascribed in the added paragraph 18 of the 4th Schedule to the Constitution by. Act 1 of 1979 being the 5th Amendment of the Constitution, it appears that all Martial Law Proclamations, Regulations, Orders, acts and actions taken up to the date of the withdrawal thereof, thus is 6th April. 1979 and the continuing acts and actions therein made up to 9th April, 1979 have been saved and ratified by the Parliament by Act I of 1979 under the 5th Amendment of the Constitution being the added paragraph 18 of the 4th schedule to the Constitution. In this connection reference may be made to the relevant provision of clause (3) of Article 225 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1962 where under the Constitution itself specifically saved certain Martial Law Regulations be transforming them into Acts of competent Legislatures under the Constitution. In the instant case of Bangladesh none of the Martial Law Proclamations baying suspended. superseded, repealed or abrogated the entire Constitution as a whole, the question of retaining any Martial Law Regulations and Orders in the body of the Constitution as normal law of the land never arose, 

 5. In this connection it may be mentioned that although by the last Proclamation of Martial Law issued on 6th April, 1979 and published in the official gazette on 7th April, 1979, Martial Law was finally withdrawn with effect from 8 P.M. of 6th April 1979. Act I of 1979 passed by the Parliament and receiving Assent of the President on 6th April, 1979 being the 5th Amendment of the Constitution adding paragraph 18 to the 4th Schedule of the Constitution, saved and ratified all acts and actions of the Martial Law administration even after the final withdrawal of Martial Law up to 9th April, 1979. This extended period between 6th April, 1979 when Martial Law was finally withdrawn and 9th April, 1979, was evidently intended to allow some time, however short it might be, to the surviving authorities of the Martial Law administration like the review authorities as per clauses (e) and (f) of the last Proclamation of Martial Law to complete the task assigned to them there under. This clearly implies that the review authorities under clauses (e) and (f) of the last Proclamation of Martial Law were obliged to complete the pending continuing proceedings of Martial Law Courts by making a final review order thereon within 9th April, 1979 at the latest, since thereafter no act or action of any continuing surviving authorities of Martial Law administration like the review authorities herein have been saved and ratified by the Parliament under Act I of 1979 being the 5th Amendment to the Constitution by way of addition of paragraph 18 to the 4th Schedule of the Constitution. This invariably means that any order made by the reviewing authorities under clauses (e) and (f) of the last Proclamation of Martial Law beyond 9th April, 1979 was not mandated by Parliament under Act I of 1979 and consequently such Act and action would under any circumstances be acts and actions without any lawful authority with no legal effect lacking constitutional sanction.
